mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with increased consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increase, or HOUST increase does not correlate with economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease does not correlate with reduced corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the real GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy coupled with weak economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with weak growth
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous 3 months signals robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases in 3 months
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and labor market
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of RSAFS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, it signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with accommodative policy effects.
